what: Head-to-head decision parity: PALADIN reference Python engine vs a standard Open Policy Agent (OPA) runtime evaluating the SAME rules-as-data policies via generic .rego evaluators.
design: rules-as-data: policies/{rbac.yaml,abac_rules.yaml,trac_rules.yaml} are loaded as `data`; policies/rego/{rbac,abac,tsphol}.rego are generic evaluators with no rule-specific logic. Editing the YAML updates both the Python engine and OPA.
scope: Parity is on the rule-evaluation layers (S3 RBAC / S4 ABAC / S6 TRAC). The S5 fact transformer (BM25 domain inference + VerbNet action classification) runs in Python and supplies both engines the same typed predicates as input.

rbac.method: opa eval vs Python, 20 tasks x 6 personas

tsphol_trac.method: opa eval on policies/rego/tsphol.rego, unique bundles from 600-row replay

live_server.note: opa run --server loaded all 6 policy files; live RBAC query -> DENY, live TRAC query -> DENY via capability_coverage, over OPA REST Data API.

reproduce: TRAC parity: python scripts/_opa_rule_parity.py (expects opa.exe in TEMP).
note_stale: app/services/opa_comparison.py + opa_engine.py is a SEPARATE, stale Python 'OPA-emulator' BASELINE that still reconstructs OLD-engine predicates (alignment_score, SelectionToleranceActive, TaskBundleDomainMismatch) from cached final_decision. It is NOT the real-OPA parity above and should not be cited for the substrate-portability claim.
